instruction:
You are tasked with designing a Verilog module for a 4-bit synchronizer flip-flop with a single asynchronous reset. The module should have the following ports:
- D: 4-bit output port
- Q: 4-bit input port
- m_aclk: input clock port
- AR: asynchronous reset port

The module should use a parameterized 1:64 synchronizer flip-flop. The input port Q should be synchronized with the input clock m_aclk and then stored in the output port D. The output port D should be updated on the rising edge of the input clock m_aclk. The module should have a single asynchronous reset port AR, which should reset the output port D to 0 when asserted.

You should use the following Verilog code snippet as a starting point for your design:

```
module system_auto_cc_0_synchronizer_ff__parameterized1_64
   (D,
    Q,
    m_aclk,
    AR);
  output [3:0]D;
  input [3:0]Q;
  input m_aclk;
  input [0:0]AR;

  wire [0:0]AR;
  wire [3:0]Q;
  (* async_reg = "true" *) (* msgon = "true" *) wire [3:0]Q_reg;
  wire m_aclk;

  assign D[3:0] = Q_reg;
  (* ASYNC_REG *) 
  (* KEEP = "yes" *) 
  (* msgon = "true" *) 
  FDCE #(
    .INIT(1'b0)) 
    \Q_reg_reg[0] 
       (.C(m_aclk),
        .CE(1'b1),
        .CLR(AR),
        .D(Q[0]),
        .Q(Q_reg[0]));
  (* ASYNC_REG *) 
  (* KEEP = "yes" *) 
  (* msgon = "true" *) 
  FDCE #(
    .INIT(1'b0)) 
    \Q_reg_reg[1] 
       (.C(m_aclk),
        .CE(1'b1),
        .CLR(AR),
        .D(Q[1]),
        .Q(Q_reg[1]));
  (* ASYNC_REG *) 
  (* KEEP = "yes" *) 
  (* msgon = "true" *) 
  FDCE #(
    .INIT(1'b0)) 
    \Q_reg_reg[2] 
       (.C(m_aclk),
        .CE(1'b1),
        .CLR(AR),
        .D(Q[2]),
        .Q(Q_reg[2]));
  (* ASYNC_REG *) 
  (* KEEP = "yes" *) 
  (* msgon = "true" *) 
  FDCE #(
    .INIT(1'b0)) 
    \Q_reg_reg[3] 
       (.C(m_aclk),
        .CE(1'b1),
        .CLR(AR),
        .D(Q[3]),
        .Q(Q_reg[3]));
endmodule
```
